The ASR runner verifies WAV checksums and\nsupports `--limit` and `--model-dir`. The translation runner uses correct Armenian\nreferences, not ASR output, and computes corpus chrF++ with SacreBLEU. Both default\nto two passes, reuse a single loaded model and retain three research examples in\noptional local reports. On the tested machine, 10 is the Realtek speakers loopback,\nPCM16 stereo at native 48 kHz. Device IDs may change. `--duration 10` limits a test;\notherwise stop with Ctrl+C. Play audio through the selected output to see levels.\nAn idle render endpoint can deliver zero callbacks; waiting is normal. The bounded\nqueue drops incoming blocks on overload with explicit counters; callback errors or\nunexpected stream closure are visible errors. Raw clock accuracy remains unvalidated.\nNo automatic device switching or synthetic silence is introduced.\n\nFor live Armenian/English pairs from this source:\n\n```powershell\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --device 10 --live\n```\n\nWait for `System Audio live active`, then play Armenian audio through the selected\noutput. Pairs use the source label `System`; microphone live still uses `Me`.\nModels load once before capture. Default live output is quiet; `--diagnostics`\nrestores levels, timings and JSON summaries. The same local FastConformer INT8,\nNLLB greedy, ASR-fragment guard, bounded phrase queue and shutdown deadline apply.\nLive accepts mono/stereo endpoints only; it converts native PCM to mono 16 kHz.\nUse the microphone's existing VAD/segment flags to tune live segmentation.\n\nWhen callbacks stop, normally 650 ms without delivered blocks finalizes the real buffered\nPCM, without inserting silence. A new burst resets VAD/resampling so separate\nplaybacks do not join. For large configured blocks, the wait is at least two block\ndurations so normal callback cadence does not look like an idle gap.\nLost frames/driver epochs remain gaps; gap phrases are skipped.\nSession display times for System are callback-receipt estimates and preserve idle\npauses (`timeline_source=callback_receipt_estimate`); raw anchors are kept, physical\nclock accuracy is unvalidated. Output order follows dispatch,\nnot a global chronological sort; each source retains its own FIFO order. Timestamps\nshare a capture-session origin but remain callback estimates, not calibrated ADC time.\n\nEach source has its own bounded pending phrase queue (`--pending-per-source`, default\n2), so one source cannot occupy the other's slots. Dispatch alternates when both\nwait. At most `--queue-size` (default 2) jobs are admitted to the shared worker,\nincluding its current job; an already admitted job is not preempted. Overflow drops\nincoming phrases for that source with warnings/counters. Raw and phrase losses,\npending wait and worker wait are separate diagnostic counters. NLLB resolves a prepared local snapshot and passes its directory to\\nTransformers, avoiding an unwanted metadata request when loading by repository ID.\\n\\nWAV inference is sequential. Current defaults in `VADConfig`:\\n\\n| Setting | Value / behavior |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Start / continuation probabilities | 0.65 / 0.50 (hysteresis) |\\n| Start confirmation | 160 ms consecutively above the start threshold |\\n| Pre-roll | Up to 300 ms before the first positive window |\\n| Minimum speech | 300 ms, also required for new candidates on Ctrl+C/duration/EOF |\\n| Short-utterance end decision | 600 ms below continuation threshold, quantized to windows (608 ms) |\\n| Preferred long-fragment boundary | After 3.5 s including pre-roll, use a 256 ms pause |\\n| Kept trailing silence | Up to 100 ms after the last positive window |\\n| Maximum segment | 6 s including padding; contiguous continuation, no overlap |\\n| Ctrl+C / duration | Close capture, drain bounded raw queue, flush resampler and final window |\\n\\nFinal partial windows are zero-padded only for VAD scoring; emitted PCM never gains\\nfabricated samples. The parent\r\nrecords the endpoint immediately after the paired HY/EN print/flush; suppressed\r\nresults have no output endpoint. The normal microphone command remains unchanged.\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m scripts.check_live_latency --repeat 2 --capture-device 9 --report reports/stage24_replay_5min.json\r\npoetry run python -m scripts.check_live_shutdown --device 9 --seconds 5 --report reports/stage24_ctrlc.json\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe first command delivers the 15 existing WAVs twice at their nominal sample rate\r\nand concurrently monitors the physical microphone under inference load. Model audio\r\ncomes from the files; microphone PCM is discarded after counting. This is an\r\nannotated replay and microphone health test, not an acoustic microphone E2E test.\r\nIt does not play sound or save new audio/transcripts. The second command checks a\r\nreal Windows CTRL_C_EVENT in a private hidden console and records resource cleanup.\r\n\r\n`data/latency_endpoints.json` contains provisional endpoint intervals from visual\r\nwaveform review, independent of Silero. `human_verified=false` is deliberate: the\r\nintervals still need listening confirmation. Do not change it without reviewing\r\nthe recordings. A local listening page for this run is\r\n`reports/stage24_endpoint_review.html`. The user chose to skip that listening\r\nreview for this audit; the labels remain provisional, not phonetic gold.\r\n\r\nThe replay report includes mean/p50/p95/p99/max, every exceedance/missing endpoint,\r\nannotation uncertainty, raw numeric stage timestamps, queue losses, memory samples,\r\npower state and capture counters. E2E begins at the reference speech end, so it\r\nincludes audio delivery/VAD hangover, dispatch, queue, WAV preparation, ASR, MT and\r\nterminal handoff/flush. Empty/filtered/dropped/unfinished output does not become a\r\nfast successful sample. Earlier forced cuts remain separate from natural ends.\r\n\r\nPortAudio stream time is calibrated against perf_counter using bracketed reads.\r\nThe read bracket bounds that clock query only, not physical ADC accuracy. On this\r\nmachine a real WASAPI probe reported ADC timestamps about 10 ms in the future\r\nrelative to callback entry. No guessed correction is applied. Physical microphone\r\nlatency cannot be certified from those timestamps or from file replay alone; the\r\nreport explicitly retains `physical_latency_certified=false`. Stage 2.4 acceptance\r\nrequires reviewed speech endpoints and an independently checked physical timeline.\r\n\r\nAfter explicit user authorization for audible playback, the acoustic probe is:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m scripts.check_acoustic_latency --input-device 9 --output-device 8 --report reports/stage24_acoustic.json\r\n```\r\n\r\nIt plays six existing WAVs at the current Windows volume and sends actual microphone\r\nPCM to the normal VAD/ASR/MT path. Waveform correlation locates each reference in\r\nthe captured signal independently of VAD; weak/ambiguous alignments are rejected.\r\nRecorded PCM stays in a bounded RAM buffer and is never written to disk. This is a\r\nmicrophone test, not Stage 3 system-loopback capture. It still retains the ADC and\r\nannotation limitations, so an acoustic run alone does not certify physical <=5 s.\r\nFor an explicit level-controlled repeat, `--samples 001.wav 003.wav 006.wav --peak 0.3`\r\nnormalizes only the test WAV peaks; it does not change Windows volume. Gain values\r\nand captured signal levels are recorded numerically. Both actual runs failed to\r\nobtain reliable reference alignment; they are retained as unsuccessful measurements.\r\nThe repeat opens both streams before starting capture to avoid blocking on output\r\nstream initialization while input blocks are already arriving. Unmatched references\r\nremain in the expected-case denominator. Probe exit 0 means the procedure completed,\r\nnot that the latency target passed; inspect the evaluation and certification fields.\r\n\r\n\r\nThe first Ctrl+C requests a stop without interrupting IPC or terminal printing:\r\nclose microphone, drain bounded raw input, finalize VAD, offer the remainder, then\r\nfinish accepted work. Queue-full rules also apply to that final remainder. The worker\r\nignores Ctrl+C so its current operation can finish. A separate small control pipe\r\ncarries the accepted-job count, avoiding a stop sentinel stuck behind a full queue.\r\nAt the deadline, terminate/kill and report unfinished jobs; a second Ctrl+C requests\r\nforced shutdown. Forced/error shutdown returns nonzero; ordinary Ctrl+C returns 130\r\nfrom Python (Poetry's parent exit-code caveat above still applies).\r\n\r\nPer-result timing separates queue wait, ASR and MT. `VAD-decision→output` excludes\r\nspeech-to-VAD hangover and is **not** speech-end latency. Hardware clock calibration\r\nand the per-phrase ≤5 s criterion remain Stage 2.4 work.\r\n\r\nAn offline integration helper feeds known speech through VAD and the real worker:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m scripts.check_live_pipeline --limit 3 --report reports/stage2_live_worker_replay.json\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse the module form for its `scripts` namespace imports. It deliberately paces job\r\nsubmission and does not emulate a live microphone or establish a latency guarantee.\r\nFor a bounded concurrent-load check, add `--microphone-device 9`: known WAV jobs\r\nare submitted before a real 5 s capture, which can also submit microphone phrases.\r\nThis mixed test has different source timelines and is not a speech-end latency test.\r\n\r\n## Validation and measurements\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp .cache/pytest\r\npoetry run ruff check .\r\npoetry check\r\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.benchmark --passes 2 --report reports/vana_asr_current.json\r\npoetry run python scripts/check_translation.py --manifest data/local/fleurs/manifest.jsonl --offline --report reports/nllb_current.json\r\n```\r\n\r\nRun inference benchmarks sequentially. The ASR runner verifies WAV checksums and\r\nsupports `--limit` and `--model-dir`. The translation runner uses correct Armenian\r\nreferences, not ASR output, and computes corpus chrF++ with SacreBLEU. Both default\r\nto two passes, reuse a single loaded model and retain three research examples in\r\noptional local reports. The regular WAV CLI saves numeric metrics only.\r\nUse `python -m pytest`: the standalone `pytest` entry point does not resolve this\r\nrepository's `tests`/`scripts` namespace imports in the current environment.\r\nThe explicit temporary directory also avoids a sandbox Windows Temp permission\r\nfailure seen with the default pytest temporary root; the cache plugin is disabled\r\nin the verified command. No application workaround is needed.\r\n\r\nVerified Stage 1 results before cleanup (15 FLEURS WAVs / correct reference texts):\r\n\r\n| Measurement | Recorded result |\r\n| --- | ---: |\r\n| ASR WER / CER | 6.67% / 2.03% |\r\n| ASR-only mean, second pass | 0.139 s |\r\n| NLLB reference-text chrF++ | 57.86 |\r\n| Full WAV mean / maximum | 1.660 / 2.805 s |\r\n| Full WAV RTF / sampled peak RSS | 0.1792 / 3076.56 MiB |\r\n\r\nAfter cleanup, 2026-10-30: **16 tests passed**, Ruff and `poetry check` passed.\r\nAll 15 WAVs completed offline: mean **2.102 s**, maximum **3.432 s**, RTF **0.2270**,\r\nRSS **3076.07 MiB**, unchanged WER/CER. The slower timings are a separate observation,\r\nnot a replacement for the earlier benchmark or proof of a cleanup-induced slowdown.\r\nThe repeated translation-only test recorded battery power, unlike the original AC runs.\r\nDetailed checks and post-cleanup benchmark results are in [TESTS.md](TESTS.md).\r\n\r\nFile timing includes WAV decoding, ASR, translation and HY/EN printing; model loading,\r\nscoring and report writing are separate. RSS is sampled every 50 ms. WER/CER use NFC,\r\ncase folding, Unicode punctuation removal and whitespace collapsing, then corpus scoring.\r\n**These measurements on ready WAVs do not prove live latency ≤5 seconds after speech.**\r\nThe 15 read-speech samples are not independent conversational validation; semantic,\r\nname and number errors remain. See [ASR_COMPARISON.md](ASR_COMPARISON.md) and\r\n[TRANSLATION_COMPARISON.md](TRANSLATION_COMPARISON.md) for historical evidence.\r\n\r\n## System Audio capture — Stage 3.1\r\n\r\nWindows uses pinned PyAudioWPatch 0.2.12.9 for WASAPI loopback. It is a separate\r\nmonitoring command by default, with no VAD/ASR/translation or saved recording:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --list-devices\r\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --device 10\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse the loopback ID from this command's list; it is not a sounddevice microphone\r\nor output-device ID. On the tested machine, 10 is the Realtek speakers loopback,\r\nPCM16 stereo at native 48 kHz. Device IDs may change. `--duration 10` limits a test;\r\notherwise stop with Ctrl+C. Play audio through the selected output to see levels.\r\nAn idle render endpoint can deliver zero callbacks; waiting is normal. The bounded\r\nqueue drops incoming blocks on overload with explicit counters; callback errors or\r\nunexpected stream closure are visible errors. Raw clock accuracy remains unvalidated.\r\nNo automatic device switching or synthetic silence is introduced.\r\n\r\nFor live Armenian/English pairs from this source:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --device 10 --live\r\n```\r\n\r\nWait for `System Audio live active`, then play Armenian audio through the selected\r\noutput. Pairs use the source label `System`; microphone live still uses `Me`.\r\nModels load once before capture. Default live output is quiet; `--diagnostics`\r\nrestores levels, timings and JSON summaries. The same local FastConformer INT8,\r\nNLLB greedy, ASR-fragment guard, bounded phrase queue and shutdown deadline apply.\r\nLive accepts mono/stereo endpoints only; it converts native PCM to mono 16 kHz.\r\nUse the microphone's existing VAD/segment flags to tune live segmentation.\r\n\r\nWhen callbacks stop, normally 650 ms without delivered blocks finalizes the real buffered\r\nPCM, without inserting silence. A new burst resets VAD/resampling so separate\r\nplaybacks do not join. For large configured blocks, the wait is at least two block\r\ndurations so normal callback cadence does not look like an idle gap.\r\nLost frames/driver epochs remain gaps; gap phrases are skipped.\r\nSession display times for System are callback-receipt estimates and preserve idle\r\npauses (`timeline_source=callback_receipt_estimate`); raw anchors are kept, physical\r\nclock accuracy is unvalidated. Silence inside delivered PCM still uses normal VAD.\r\nCtrl+C closes capture, drains/finalizes, and gives accepted inference up to 15 s.\r\nNo permanent audio/transcript log is created; the existing short-lived ASR WAV\r\nbridge is reused and cleaned up.\r\n\r\nThe individual commands still run one source each. To run both through one model worker:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --list-devices\r\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --microphone-device 9 --device 10\r\n```\r\n\r\nHere `--microphone-device` is the sounddevice input ID and `--device` is the\r\nPyAudioWPatch loopback ID. Both must be selected explicitly. Combined mode is always\r\nlive; models load once, with separate VAD/resampler states and raw queues per source.\r\n`Me`/`System` labels travel with each inference job. Output order follows dispatch,\r\nnot a global chronological sort; each source retains its own FIFO order. Timestamps\r\nshare a capture-session origin but remain callback estimates, not calibrated ADC time.\r\n\r\nEach source has its own bounded pending phrase queue (`--pending-per-source`, default\r\n2), so one source cannot occupy the other's slots. Dispatch alternates when both\r\nwait. At most `--queue-size` (default 2) jobs are admitted to the shared worker,\r\nincluding its current job; an already admitted job is not preempted. Overflow drops\r\nincoming phrases for that source with warnings/counters. Raw and phrase losses,\r\npending wait and worker wait are separate diagnostic counters. Fair dispatch cannot\r\nguarantee <=5 s when the CPU is overloaded.\r\n\r\nCtrl+C closes both streams, drains/finalizes both raw/VAD paths, then drains pending\r\nand admitted work within one shared shutdown deadline (default 15 s). Errors in\r\neither input/worker stop both; timeout cancels pending work and terminates inference\r\nwith explicit unfinished counters. `--diagnostics` enables periodic source summaries;\r\nordinary output stays quiet. If an output device changes, list/select the intended\r\nIDs and restart; the program does not silently switch endpoints. If the microphone\r\nhears the speakers, the same audio can appear under both source labels; headphones\r\ncan avoid that acoustic duplication. There is no echo cancellation/deduplication.\r\nSpeaker Diarization remains Stage 4.\r\n\r\n## Repository and AI history\r\n\r\nWeights, audio, references, reports, `.venv`, cache and `.env` files are ignored by Git.\r\nCleanup removes implementations, not prior results, model caches, test data or Git history.\r\nKeep every actual Codex session in full, unedited, and export each to its own Markdown\r\nfile in `chats/` before submission. WER/CER use NFC,\\r\\ncase folding, Unicode punctuation removal and whitespace collapsing, then corpus scoring.\\r\\n**These measurements on ready WAVs do not prove live latency ≤5 seconds after speech.**\\r\\nThe 15 read-speech samples are not independent conversational validation; semantic,\\r\\nname and number errors remain. See [ASR_COMPARISON.md](ASR_COMPARISON.md) and\\r\\n[TRANSLATION_COMPARISON.md](TRANSLATION_COMPARISON.md) for historical evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\n## System Audio capture — Stage 3.1\\r\\n\\r\\nWindows uses pinned PyAudioWPatch 0.2.12.9 for WASAPI loopback. It is a separate\\r\\nmonitoring command by default, with no VAD/ASR/translation or saved recording:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --list-devices\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --device 10\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the loopback ID from this command's list; it is not a sounddevice microphone\\r\\nor output-device ID. On the tested machine, 10 is the Realtek speakers loopback,\\r\\nPCM16 stereo at native 48 kHz. Device IDs may change. `--duration 10` limits a test;\\r\\notherwise stop with Ctrl+C. Play audio through the selected output to see levels.\\r\\nAn idle render endpoint can deliver zero callbacks; waiting is normal. The bounded\\r\\nqueue drops incoming blocks on overload with explicit counters; callback errors or\\r\\nunexpected stream closure are visible errors. Raw clock accuracy remains unvalidated.\\r\\nNo automatic device switching or synthetic silence is introduced.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor live Armenian/English pairs from this source:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --device 10 --live\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWait for `System Audio live active`, then play Armenian audio through the selected\\r\\noutput. Pairs use the source label `System`; microphone live still uses `Me`.\\r\\nModels load once before capture. Default live output is quiet; `--diagnostics`\\r\\nrestores levels, timings and JSON summaries. The same local FastConformer INT8,\\r\\nNLLB greedy, ASR-fragment guard, bounded phrase queue and shutdown deadline apply.\\r\\nLive accepts mono/stereo endpoints only; it converts native PCM to mono 16 kHz.\\r\\nUse the microphone's existing VAD/segment flags to tune live segmentation.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen callbacks stop, normally 650 ms without delivered blocks finalizes the real buffered\\r\\nPCM, without inserting silence. A new burst resets VAD/resampling so separate\\r\\nplaybacks do not join. For large configured blocks, the wait is at least two block\\r\\ndurations so normal callback cadence does not look like an idle gap.\\r\\nLost frames/driver epochs remain gaps; gap phrases are skipped.\\r\\nSession display times for System are callback-receipt estimates and preserve idle\\r\\npauses (`timeline_source=callback_receipt_estimate`); raw anchors are kept, physical\\r\\nclock accuracy is unvalidated. Silence inside delivered PCM still uses normal VAD.\\r\\nCtrl+C closes capture, drains/finalizes, and gives accepted inference up to 15 s.\\r\\nNo permanent audio/transcript log is created; the existing short-lived ASR WAV\\r\\nbridge is reused and cleaned up.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe individual commands still run one source each. To run both through one model worker:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --list-devices\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --microphone-device 9 --device 10\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nHere `--microphone-device` is the sounddevice input ID and `--device` is the\\r\\nPyAudioWPatch loopback ID. Both must be selected explicitly. Combined mode is always\\r\\nlive; models load once, with separate VAD/resampler states and raw queues per source.\\r\\n`Me`/`System` labels travel with each inference job. Output order follows dispatch,\\r\\nnot a global chronological sort; each source retains its own FIFO order. Timestamps\\r\\nshare a capture-session origin but remain callback estimates, not calibrated ADC time.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach source has its own bounded pending phrase queue (`--pending-per-source`, default\\r\\n2), so one source cannot occupy the other's slots. Dispatch alternates when both\\r\\nwait. At most `--queue-size` (default 2) jobs are admitted to the shared worker,\\r\\nincluding its current job; an already admitted job is not preempted. Overflow drops\\r\\nincoming phrases for that source with warnings/counters. Raw and phrase losses,\\r\\npending wait and worker wait are separate diagnostic counters. Fair dispatch cannot\\r\\nguarantee <=5 s when the CPU is overloaded.\\r\\n\\r\\nCtrl+C closes both streams, drains/finalizes both raw/VAD paths, then drains pending\\r\\nand admitted work within one shared shutdown deadline (default 15 s). Errors in\\r\\neither input/worker stop both; timeout cancels pending work and terminates inference\\r\\nwith explicit unfinished counters. `--diagnostics` enables periodic source summaries;\\r\\nordinary output stays quiet. If an output device changes, list/select the intended\\r\\nIDs and restart; the program does not silently switch endpoints. If the microphone\\r\\nhears the speakers, the same audio can appear under both source labels; headphones\\r\\ncan avoid that acoustic duplication. There is no echo cancellation/deduplication.\\r\\nSpeaker Diarization remains Stage 4.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Repository and AI history\\r\\n\\r\\nWeights, audio, references, reports, `.venv`, cache and `.env` files are ignored by Git.\\r\\nCleanup removes implementations, not prior results, model caches, test data or Git history.\\r\\nKeep every actual Codex session in full, unedited, and export each to its own Markdown\\r\\nfile in `chats/` before submission. Summaries and handovers do not replace these exports.\\r\\n# Decisions\\r\\n\\r\\nChronological record. Full actual Codex exports remain required before submission.\\r\\nNo commit was created during this cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Stage 2 acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\nStage 2.1–2.3 implementation and actual results are recorded below.\\r\\nStage 2.4 remains planned; its latency acceptance criteria are not yet satisfied.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1 Microphone Capture\\r\\n\\r\\n- Enumerate input devices and select one explicitly; verify invalid/unavailable\\r\\n  devices fail clearly. Confirm actual sample rate, channels and buffer format.\\r\\n- Capture continuously for an agreed test interval with counters/status for dropped\\r\\n  audio or device errors. First step runs without VAD and ASR/translation models.\\r\\n- Ctrl+C closes the stream and releases the device; another capture can start.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.2 VAD + Segmentation\\r\\n\\r\\n- On known speech/silence input, check speech start/end, silence-only behavior,\\r\\n  short pauses, utterance edges and absence of lost or duplicated samples.\\r\\n- Verify pre-roll, trailing silence and a maximum segment length agreed in the plan;\\r\\n  define handling of long speech and partial final buffers. Check real device format\\r\\n  conversion against the chosen VAD and ASR requirements.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3 Producer–Consumer Pipeline\\r\\n\\r\\n- Slow inference must not block the audio callback/capture. Reuse loaded\\r\\n  FastConformer and NLLB instances; preserve terminal HY/EN output and WAV CLI.\\r\\n- Use a bounded queue of completed segments. Test full queue and prolonged slow\\r\\n  consumer; the approved overflow policy must be explicit and observable, with\\r\\n  queue depth/wait and any dropped segments counted. Memory must stay bounded.\\r\\n- Ctrl+C stops producers and worker without deadlock; define queued/in-progress\\r\\n  segment handling and propagate errors without hidden fallback.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.4 Live Latency Testing\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use a monotonic timeline mapped to capture samples. \\\"translation_revision\\\": translator.revision,\\r\\n    }\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\ndef asr_fragment_reason(text: str) -> str | None:\\r\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Reject isolated letter fragments, not short words or numbers.\\r\\n\\r\\n    This is a structural live-output guard, not a confidence/meaning detector.\\r\\n    Preserve Armenian single-letter words; casefold also expands Armenian ligatures.\\r\\n finished = perf_counter()\\r\\n    return {\\r\\n        \\\"kind\\\": \\\"result\\\", \\\"sequence\\\": job.sequence,\\r\\n        \\\"speaker\\\": job.speaker,\\r\\n        \\\"armenian\\\": 16000,\\r\\n        \\\"duration_s\\\": duration, \\\"source\\\": segment.metadata(),\\r\\n        \\\"enqueued_monotonic\\\": job.enqueued_monotonic, \\\"dequeued_monotonic\\\": dequeued,\\r\\n finally:\\r\\n        events.close()\\r\\n        control.close()\\r\\n        jobs.close()\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\nclass InferenceWorker:\\r\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"One producer, capacity-limited jobs, and a None,\\r\\n        speaker: str = \\\"Me\\\",\\r\\n        speaker_factory=None,\\r\\n    ) -> None:\\r\\n        if capacity < 1 or not math.isfinite(shutdown_timeout) or shutdown_timeout <= 0:\\r\\n diagnostics\\r\\n        self.on_result = on_result\\r\\n        self.context = mp.get_context(\\\"spawn\\\")\\r\\n        self.jobs = self.context.Queue(maxsize=capacity)\\r\\n        self.events, None\\r\\n        self.session_dir: Path | None = None\\r\\n        self.closed = False\\r\\n        self.ready = False\\r\\n        self._eof = False\\r\\n        self.error: str | None = None\\r\\n \\\"peak_queue_depth\\\": 0, \\\"max_queue_wait_s\\\": 0.0, \\\"sum_queue_wait_s\\\": 0.0,\\r\\n            \\\"sum_asr_s\\\": 0.0, \\\"sum_translation_s\\\": 0.0,\\r\\n            \\\"max_decision_to_output_s\\\": 0.0, \\\"forced_termination\\\": False,\\r\\n            \\\"discarded_on_shutdown\\\": 0, \\\"worker_exitcode\\\": None,\\r\\n            \\\"result_parts\\\": (\\\"session-\\\" + uuid4().hex)\\r\\n        self.session_dir.mkdir()\\r\\n        self.process = self.context.Process(\\r\\n            target=_worker_main,\\r\\n            args=(self.config, name=\\\"armenian-inference\\\",\\r\\n        )\\r\\n        try:\\r\\n            self.process.start()\\r\\n            self._sender.close()\\r\\n            self._control.close()\\r\\n disagrees with its sample bounds.\\\")\\r\\n        try:\\r\\n            self.jobs.put_nowait(InferenceJob(sequence, segment, perf_counter(), speaker))\\r\\n        except Full:\\r\\n 1. Для каждой ячейки видеть причину Unknown или нового ID, длительность, RMS, сходство половин, два лучших совпадения и изменение центроида.
2. На существующих публичных файлах сравнить одинаковый вход с диагностикой и без неё: метки, границы и PCM должны совпасть.
3. Отдельно проверить короткие ответы, возврат голоса, смены без пауз и влияние уровня/канала. Синтетические изменения будут только проверкой чувствительности.
4. Менять алгоритм лишь после воспроизводимого сбоя и сравнения, которое учитывает и лишние ID, и ошибочное слияние людей.

Для событий добавлю отдельный opt-in флаг: он не будет включать посекундные уровни. Пороги, склейку и фильтры пока оставляю прежними.

self.first_frame = block.start_frame\n        self.last_received = block.received_monotonic\n        self.wait_s = max(self.idle_s, 2 * block.frames / self.rate)\n        result.extend(self._stamp(self.processor.push(block)))\n        return result\n\n    def idle(self, now, final_frame, capture_epoch):\n        if self.processor is None or now - self.last_received < Exact versions are in `poetry.lock`.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Argument | Meaning |\\r\\n| --- | --- |\\r\\n| `--wav PATH` / `--manifest PATH` | Required, mutually exclusive input |\\r\\n| `--asr-model PATH` | Prepared FastConformer directory; default `cache-dir/vana` |\\r\\n| `--cache-dir PATH` | Default `.cache/models`; NLLB uses its `translation/` subdirectory |\\r\\n| `--threads N` | Model CPU threads, default 4; ORT inter-op = 1 |\\r\\n| `--offline` | Require local files; both models already require prepared artifacts |\\r\\n| `--report PATH` | Optional numeric JSON report, without recognized text or translations |\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `poetry run armenian-speech --help` for the actual interface. Experimental model\\r\\nselection arguments were removed. Download helpers retain `--revision`; inference\\r\\nexpects the pinned revisions above, so custom revisions require an explicit code decision.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n`cli.run` validates input and initializes `OnnxArmenianASR` and `ArmenianTranslator`\\r\\nonce before the file loop. `pipeline.process_wav` invokes `transcribe(Path)` then\\r\\n`translate(text)` and `output.print_segment`, using existing `Transcriber`/`Translator`\\r\\nprotocols. `asr.py` contains the shared `Segment` dataclass; the model adapter is in\\r\\n`asr_onnx.py`. NLLB resolves a prepared local snapshot and passes its directory to\\r\\nTransformers, avoiding an unwanted metadata request when loading by repository ID.\\r\\n\\r\\nWAV inference is sequential. Its only background thread is the sampled RSS monitor.\\r\\nMicrophone diagnostics use PortAudio's callback and a bounded raw-block queue;\\r\\nthe default capture-only mode does not load models. Opt-in `--vad` uses one Silero\\r\\nONNX instance in the main consumer, with streaming PyAV resampling and bounded phrase\\r\\nbuffering. Opt-in `--live` adds a bounded phrase queue and one spawned inference\\r\\nprocess, loading FastConformer INT8/NLLB greedy once. Terminal HY/EN output stays\\r\\nin the parent. System audio and speaker identification remain unimplemented.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Microphone capture — Stage 2.1\\r\\n\\r\\nFrom the project directory, enumerate inputs, then select an explicit device index:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --list-devices\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --device 1 --duration 60\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --device 9 --sample-rate 48000\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIndices above match this machine's current Intel Microphone Array: 1 is MME,\\r\\n9 is WASAPI. Indices can change; check the list on each setup. With no `--duration`,\\r\\ncapture continues until Ctrl+C. `peak_1s` measures the latest progress interval;\\r\\n`peak_max` is the maximum since startup. Speak and pause to check the changing level.\\r\\nCtrl+C closes the stream and prints a numeric summary; Python returns 130.\\r\\nOn this Windows setup, Poetry itself returns 1 after the console interrupt even\\r\\nthough the child closes normally. For the child's own exit code, use\\r\\n`.\\\\.venv\\\\Scripts\\\\python.exe -m armenian_speech.microphone --device 9 --sample-rate 48000`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe default delivered format is mono `int16` at 16 kHz; `--channels` and\\r\\n`--sample-rate` select explicit alternatives. Unsupported settings fail without\\r\\nswitching device or rate. MME accepted 16 kHz; WASAPI required explicit 48 kHz here.\\r\\nStartup prints the opened stream's reported rate, channels, dtype and input latency;\\r\\nthese describe the application stream, not an independent measurement of ADC clocks.\\r\\nNo resampling, audio saving, VAD or ASR/translation runs in this command.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe callback copies each temporary PortAudio buffer into a 32-block queue without\\r\\nwaiting for free queue space. Main-thread diagnostics consume and discard it.\\r\\nWhen full, the incoming block is discarded and exact application-drop counters grow;\\r\\nthis raw diagnostics queue is separate from the future inference-segment queue.\\r\\nDriver overflow/underflow events are counted separately: the driver does not report\\r\\nan exact lost-frame count (`driver_lost_frames` is null). Pending frames at shutdown\\r\\nare reported and discarded. Progress counters are snapshots; final counters follow\\r\\nstream closure. Python callbacks are not a hard real-time guarantee.\\r\\n\\r\\nRaw ADC/callback times remain in PortAudio's stream clock. MME returned zeros here;\\r\\nWASAPI returned advancing ADC times approximately 10 ms after callback times.\\r\\nZero, nonfinite, nonmonotonic and future-ADC anomalies have separate counters.\\r\\nThese timestamps are not validated speech endings or live latency measurements.\\r\\nSummary ADC times describe processed blocks and can lag capture counters under load.\\r\\nClock mapping/validation remains pending. Explicit 48-to-16 kHz conversion is now\\r\\navailable in the optional Stage 2.2 VAD mode.\\r\\nReal capture and Ctrl+C evidence, including limitations, is in [TESTS.md](TESTS.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n## VAD and speech phrases — Stage 2.2\\r\\n\\r\\nSilero VAD 6.2.3 runs with the existing ONNX Runtime CPU, one thread. Its ONNX model\\r\\nand MIT license are extracted from a SHA-256-pinned upstream wheel; no wheel code\\r\\nis executed or installed. On a fresh setup, prepare it explicitly:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python scripts/download_vad.py\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe model is already prepared on this machine at `.cache/models/silero/`.\\r\\nRuntime verifies the model checksum and provenance and never downloads implicitly.\\r\\n`--vad-model PATH` selects another prepared copy of the same pinned artifact.\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --list-devices\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --device 9 --sample-rate 48000 --vad\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nSpeak, then pause for roughly a second. `p_speech` is the latest speech probability,\\r\\n`speech_candidate` indicates an active candidate, and `VAD phrase: {...}` announces\\r\\na completed segment with sample-based times and a finish reason. `--vad` remains\\r\\ndiagnostics only; use `--live` below for HY/EN.\\r\\n\\r\\nPyAV performs stateful anti-aliased resampling to mono PCM16 16 kHz. VAD accepts\\r\\nmono/stereo input; more channels fail explicitly. Each 512-sample (32 ms) window\\r\\nis normalized to float32 for Silero. Current defaults in `VADConfig`:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Setting | Value / behavior |\\r\\n| --- | --- |\\r\\n| Start / continuation probabilities | 0.65 / 0.50 (hysteresis) |\\r\\n| Start confirmation | 160 ms consecutively above the start threshold |\\r\\n| Pre-roll | Up to 300 ms before the first positive window |\\r\\n| Minimum speech | 300 ms, also required for new candidates on Ctrl+C/duration/EOF |\\r\\n| Short-utterance end decision | 600 ms below continuation threshold, quantized to windows (608 ms) |\\r\\n| Preferred long-fragment boundary | After 3.5 s including pre-roll, use a 256 ms pause |\\r\\n| Kept trailing silence | Up to 100 ms after the last positive window |\\r\\n| Maximum segment | 6 s including padding; contiguous continuation, no overlap |\\r\\n| Ctrl+C / duration | Close capture, drain bounded raw queue, flush resampler and final window |\\r\\n\\r\\nFinal partial windows are zero-padded only for VAD scoring; emitted PCM never gains\\r\\nfabricated samples. Unconfirmed/short new candidates are discarded even at shutdown;\\r\\nshort tails of an already accepted forced continuation are retained to avoid losing\\r\\nreal samples. A forced maximum can include extra silence when reached\\r\\nbefore the normal hangover expires. No full-session recording is accumulated.\\r\\nFor the shorter pause, elapsed audio is measured from the segment start through\\r\\nits last positive VAD window, including pre-roll and internal pauses. Shorter pauses\\r\\nbefore that target keep the original 600 ms rule. `reason=short_pause` identifies\\r\\nan earlier long-fragment boundary. Pre-roll of the next segment is clamped to the\\r\\nprevious segment's end so quick resumption cannot replay already emitted audio.\\r\\nSpeech without a suitable pause is split at the hard limit, which can cut a word;\\r\\nsample continuity does not guarantee recognition continuity at that boundary.\\r\\n\\r\\nQueue drops and driver overflow/underflow epochs end an incomplete segment with\\r\\n`reason=gap`, reset VAD/resampler state, and prevent joining audio across the loss.\\r\\nKnown missing frames include trailing queue loss at shutdown. Driver loss has unknown\\r\\nduration and marks subsequent sample timelines uncertain. Raw ADC, callback and\\r\\nmonotonic receipt anchors are retained, including the capture block at the estimated\\r\\nVAD speech end; a bounded anchor history accompanies the bounded PCM buffer.\\r\\n\\r\\n`vad_start_s` / `vad_end_s` are window-based VAD estimates in nominal captured-audio\\r\\ntime, not independently labelled speech boundaries. `clock_accuracy=unvalidated`\\r\\nis explicit: WASAPI timestamp anomalies and clock drift are not silently corrected.\\r\\nThe audio cap does not guarantee NLLB's 512-token limit; live translation explicitly\\r\\nsplits oversized text by words without truncation. No live ≤5 s claim follows from these checks.\\r\\n\\r\\nOffline VAD screening on the existing WAVs, without ASR/MT:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python scripts/check_vad.py --passes 2 --report reports/stage2_vad_screening.json\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis adds known silence around each WAV, verifies its checksum, streams arbitrary\\r\\nblock sizes, and saves numeric timings/segment metadata only. It measures neither\\r\\nmicrophone latency nor speech-boundary accuracy. Results and device tests are in TESTS.md.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Live transcription and translation — Stage 2.3\\r\\n\\r\\nThe models are already prepared on this machine. From the project directory:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --list-devices\\r\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.microphone --device 9 --sample-rate 48000 --live\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWait for `Inference worker ready` and `Microphone active`, then speak Armenian and\\r\\npause. Output uses the existing format: `[00:00:12] Me  HY: ...  EN: ...`.\\r\\nHY and EN always appear together after both recognition and translation finish.\\r\\nLong speech is processed in shorter audio fragments rather than waiting for the\\r\\nwhole sentence; line length is not a fixed word count. Six seconds bounds audio\\r\\naccumulation, not output latency: queue wait, ASR and translation still follow.\\r\\n`--live` includes VAD; it is mutually exclusive with the diagnostic `--vad` flag.\\r\\nModels load before opening the microphone. Live inference is always local-only.\\r\\nBefore translation, live output skips isolated letter fragments such as `Հ։`/`Հ.`\\r\\nand text containing no letters/numbers. Short words and numbers remain eligible;\\r\\nArmenian single-letter `ա`/`է` and the ligature `և` are preserved. Punctuation and\\r\\ncase are ignored only for this check; accepted text is not rewritten. A skipped\\r\\nfragment produces neither HY nor EN and never calls the translation tokenizer/model.\\r\\nASR still runs: this gate needs the recognized text and does not classify coughs,\\r\\nbreaths or other audio. Longer incorrect words/phrases can still pass.\\r\\nStandalone spelled letters/initials can be filtered; use `--allow-asr-fragments`\\r\\nto disable the guard when those are needed. Initials inside a longer name remain.\\r\\nThe diagnostic summary counts `filtered_asr_fragments` separately from `empty_asr`\\r\\nand queue drops. Filtered jobs count as completed so shutdown accounting is preserved.\\r\\nThe original WAV CLI does not use this live-only guard.\\r\\nLive output is quiet by default: startup messages, HY/EN and actionable warnings/errors.\\r\\nAdd `--diagnostics` to restore per-second levels/probabilities, inference timings,\\r\\nmodel metadata and the numeric shutdown summary. Capture-only/`--vad` remain diagnostic modes.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Live option | Default / purpose |\\r\\n| --- | --- |\\r\\n| `--cache-dir PATH` | `.cache/models`, prepared ASR/translation cache |\\r\\n| Shorter fragments can change ASR and\r\ntranslation quality at boundaries and generate more inference jobs; measure queue\r\nbacklog with `--diagnostics` when tuning. On the 15-WAV VAD+ASR comparison, these\r\nshorter settings increased WER from 6.67% to 11.67% (27 fragments instead of 16).\r\nThe nominal-rate run also exposed queue drops/timeouts under current CPU load;\r\nthe smaller audio cap is an experimental responsiveness/quality tradeoff, not a\r\nclaim of a completed live latency target. self.first_frame = block.start_frame\n        self.last_received = block.received_monotonic\n        self.wait_s = max(self.idle_s, 2 * block.frames / self.rate)\n Синтетический тест уже воспроизвёл дробление трёх голосов на пять ID при смене полосы, но для конкретных Speaker 4/5 в звонке всё ещё нужно сопоставление с голосами.

```

Speaker 4/5 в\nтекстовом логе нельзя независимо привязать к человеку или конкретной причине.\n\n## Что установлено по коду\n\n- Registry создаётся один раз в worker и сохраняется между System jobs/idle.\n  Увеличение epoch VAD само по себе его не сбрасывает.\n- Новый ID появляется после одной полной 2 s ячейки: половины согласны между\n  собой, но лучший centroid score <0.47. Отдельного подтверждения личности нет.\n- Изменение канала может дать согласованные половины одного голоса, отличающиеся\n  от его старого центроида. Проверка половин не защищает от этого механизма.\n- <1 s не получает embedding. 1–<2 s не создаёт и не обучает ID. Поэтому сессия,\n  состоящая только из коротких ответов, может вообще не зарегистрировать голос.\n- Половины имеют самостоятельный RMS gate 0.003. Вся ячейка может быть достаточно\n  громкой, но тихая половина блокирует назначение. Паузы/pre-roll тоже входят в окно;\n  2 s PCM не означает 2 s речи одного человека.\n- Присвоение ID идёт до ASR. Новый ID может не появиться в HY/EN из-за пустого\n  распознавания/существующего текстового guard. По отсутствию напечатанного номера\n  нельзя делать вывод об отсутствии регистрации.\n\n## Изменение этого шага\n\nДобавлен отдельный `--speaker-diagnostics`, требующий `--diarize`. События передаются\nдо ASR, по одной записи на ячейку, включая ячейки, позже объединённые в один part.\nОбычный режим не получает новых сообщений. Этот флаг не включает периодические\nуровни, но включает итоговый capture summary для проверки потерь/очередей.\n\n```powershell\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --microphone-device 9 --device 10 --diarize --speaker-diagnostics\n```\n\nПеред запуском остановить старый процесс Ctrl+C: worker не перечитывает код сам.\nИсходная команда без нового флага продолжает работать. Нет `--min-audio-ms`.\n\n`Speaker decision:` содержит sequence исходного job, sample bounds/время, VAD\nmetadata и reason, RMS ячейки/половин, доступность embeddings, half score, два\nлучших pre-update score и их разность, пороги, capacity, counts до/после и cosine\nизменения обученного центроида за этот шаг. Векторы и PCM не передаются в этих\nсобытиях. Числа не являются вероятностями правильной личности.\n\nПричины: `new`, `match`, `ambiguous`, `capacity`, `insufficient_evidence`,\n`embedding_unavailable`, `half_embedding_unavailable`, `half_disagreement`.\n`embedding_rejection` уточняет short/low RMS/native not-ready для полной ячейки.\n`halves_available` и `half_rms` показывают отказ половин. `registry_consulted=false`\nозначает, что показанные best/second — только диагностическое сравнение;\nпроверка половин не позволила использовать его. У короткого окна половины не\nпроверяются (`halves_available=null`). Counts — число обучающих ячеек, не реплик.\n\nГенерация событий opt-in; они не накапливаются в live worker и не сохраняются в\nфайл. Печать/IPC могут добавлять нагрузку; равенство меток на фиксированном входе\nне доказывает равенства задержки/потерь под живой нагрузкой. Capture summary нужен\nименно для проверки этой границы. Me и совместный HY/EN сохраняются.\n\n## Воспроизводимое сравнение\n\n`scripts/check_speaker_decisions.py` использует существующие checksum-verified\nпубличные LibriSpeech файлы, реальный CAMPPlus и в одном сценарии реальный Silero.\nНе открывает устройства, не запускает ASR/MT и не записывает аудио. То есть теперь причина этих Unknown видна: проверка половин и короткие остатки. Это ещё не доказывает, что всем этим фрагментам правильно присвоить Speaker 1, поэтому автоматически отменять проверку или склеивать хвосты оснований пока нет.

- Реплики второго оставались **Unknown**.
- Ты в начале и конце отображался как **Me**.

Почему второй не зарегистрировался:

|---|---:|---|

Таким образом, сейчас видны две проблемы: **регистрация голоса по коротким репликам** и **ложные отказы проверки половин у известного голоса**. Одной правкой проверки половин всё не решить.

Повторять такой же тест пока не нужно. Следующий шаг — проверить варианты регистрации короткого нового голоса отдельно от сохранения известного, с контролем лишних ID и смешения людей. В этом вложении нет финального `Capture summary:`, поэтому потери и завершение очередей здесь оценить нельзя.

Это подтверждает захват того воспроизведения,\nно не автоматически любой маршрут приложения звонка и не качество диаризации.\n\nПри смене устройства/подключении гарнитуры повторно выполнить:\n\n```powershell\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --list-devices\n```\n\n## Действующие интерфейсы и возможные причины проблемы\n\nОсновные файлы:\n\n- `src/armenian_speech/combined.py`: два источника, отдельные VAD/ресемплеры,\n  общая очередь с обслуживанием по источникам и один ASR/MT worker.\n- `src/armenian_speech/live_pipeline.py`: Windows spawn, WorkerConfig,\n  InferenceJob; System внутри worker проходит SpeakerTracker до ASR.\n  `source_label` сохраняет System для счётчиков; `speaker` — отображаемая метка.\n  Один исходный job завершается только на last_part; части выводят отдельные HY/EN.\n- `src/armenian_speech/speakers.py`: Extractor, Registry, SpeakerTracker.\n- `src/armenian_speech/loopback_vad.py`: завершение по idle без выдуманных нулей;\n  обычный idle может менять epoch VAD. Это не обязательно потеря аудио.\n- `src/armenian_speech/asr_onnx.py`: файловый transcribe(Path).\n\nВосстановленный алгоритм:\n\n1. Делит System VAD PCM на неперекрывающиеся2sячейки.\n2. Для полной ячейки дополнительно сравнивает embeddings её1sполовин;\n   при провале проверок выставляет Unknown.\n3. Extractor не выдаёт embedding для <1s и RMS<0.003.\n4. Новые ID создаются только из полной2sячейки (`learn=True`). Короткие ячейки\n   могут лишь совпасть с существующим голосом или остаться Unknown.\n5. Registry использует нормализованные embeddings, cosine threshold0.47,\n   margin0.08, максимум8centroids. Если лучший score ниже threshold, при разрешённом\n   обучении создаётся новый ID. Близкие два score дают Unknown. Нет объединения\n   дублирующих кластеров, учёта канала или подтверждения нового ID несколькими ходами.\n6. Соседние одинаковые метки склеиваются. Разные, в том числе Unknown, дают\n   самостоятельные ASR/MT-фрагменты. Это может обрывать слова/контекст.\n\nЭто объясняет **механизмы**, способные создавать много Unknown и дополнительные ID,\nно не доказывает причину каждой ошибки в звонке без аудио/сопоставления с людьми.\nНельзя объявлять Speaker3/4/5 реальными новыми участниками только по номерам.\nНельзя просто скрыть Unknown, принудительно присвоить предыдущий ID или ограничить\nчисло говорящих двумя: это может замаскировать ошибки и слить разных людей.\n\n## Последний звонок после точного возврата первой 4.2\n\nПользователь сообщает: «Спикеры со временем увеличиваются почему-то и unknown\nочень много». Speaker2 в присланных строках нет.\n  Он мог быть создан внутренне без напечатанного текста: ASR/фильтр могут подавить\n  результат. Отдельные поздние диагностические скрипты\\n`check_short_features.py` и `check_speaker_stability.py` убраны из активного scripts/;\\nих копии могут находиться в локальной страховке.\\n\\n## Запуск и проверенные устройства\\n\\nТекущая команда первой 4.2:\\n\\n```powershell\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --microphone-device 9 --device 10 --diarize\\n```\\n\\nБез `--diarize` сохраняется прежний Me/System режим. Перед проверкой новой версии\\nнужно остановить старый процесс Ctrl+C и запустить заново: загруженный worker\\nсам не перечитывает изменённый исходный код.\\n\\nУстройства проверялись повторно в обычной среде Windows:\\n\\n- sounddevice input9: **Microphone Array (Intel Smart Sound Technology for Digital\\n  Microphones), WASAPI**, встроенный микрофон, 48 kHz.\\n- PyAudioWPatch loopback10: **Speakers (Realtek(R) Audio) [Loopback]**, 48 kHz stereo.\\n- Это две отдельные системы нумерации. Устройство9 не означает микрофон гарнитуры.\\n- Один раз пользователь получил пустой список loopback. Причина не установлена.\\n  При повторном опросе вне песочницы loopback10 появился и успешно открылся.\\n  Список внутри песочницы отличался от обычной среды Windows.\\n\\nПользователь подтвердил поступление реального системного звука командой:\\n\\n```powershell\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.system_audio --device 10 --duration 10\\n```\\n\\nРезультат:469blocks,480256frames,10.0053s аудио, peak0.0999146,\\nstatus_events=0, input_overflows=0, queue_dropped_frames=0, все кадры обработаны,\\npending_frames=0, поток закрыт. Это подтверждает захват того воспроизведения,\\nно не автоматически любой маршрут приложения звонка и не качество диаризации.\\n\\nПри смене устройства/подключении гарнитуры повторно выполнить:\\n\\n```powershell\\npoetry run python -m armenian_speech.combined --list-devices\\n```\\n\\n## Действующие интерфейсы и возможные причины проблемы\\n\\nОсновные файлы:\\n\\n- `src/armenian_speech/combined.py`: два источника, отдельные VAD/ресемплеры,\\n  общая очередь с обслуживанием по источникам и один ASR/MT worker.\\n- `src/armenian_speech/live_pipeline.py`: Windows spawn, WorkerConfig,\\n  InferenceJob; System внутри worker проходит SpeakerTracker до ASR.\\n  `source_label` сохраняет System для счётчиков; `speaker` — отображаемая метка.\\n  Один исходный job завершается только на last_part; части выводят отдельные HY/EN.\\n- `src/armenian_speech/speakers.py`: Extractor, Registry, SpeakerTracker.\\n- `src/armenian_speech/loopback_vad.py`: завершение по idle без выдуманных нулей;\\n  обычный idle может менять epoch VAD. Это не обязательно потеря аудио.\\n- `src/armenian_speech/asr_onnx.py`: файловый transcribe(Path).\\n\\nВосстановленный алгоритм:\\n\\n1. Делит System VAD PCM на неперекрывающиеся2sячейки.\\n2. Для полной ячейки дополнительно сравнивает embeddings её1sполовин;\\n   при провале проверок выставляет Unknown.\\n3. Extractor не выдаёт embedding для <1s и RMS<0.003.\\n4. Новые ID создаются только из полной2sячейки (`learn=True`). Короткие ячейки\\n   могут лишь совпасть с существующим голосом или остаться Unknown.\\n5. Registry использует нормализованные embeddings, cosine threshold0.47,\\n   margin0.08, максимум8centroids. Если лучший score ниже threshold, при разрешённом\\n   обучении создаётся новый ID. Близкие два score дают Unknown. Нет объединения\\n   дублирующих кластеров, учёта канала или подтверждения нового ID несколькими ходами.\\n6. Соседние одинаковые метки склеиваются. Разные, в том числе Unknown, дают\\n   самостоятельные ASR/MT-фрагменты. Это может обрывать слова/контекст.\\n\\nЭто объясняет **механизмы**, способные создавать много Unknown и дополнительные ID,\\nно не доказывает причину каждой ошибки в звонке без аудио/сопоставления с людьми.\\nНельзя объявлять Speaker3/4/5 реальными новыми участниками только по номерам.\\nНельзя просто скрыть Unknown, принудительно присвоить предыдущий ID или ограничить\\nчисло говорящих двумя: это может замаскировать ошибки и слить разных людей.\\n\\n## Последний звонок после точного возврата первой 4.2\\n\\nПользователь сообщает: «Спикеры со временем увеличиваются почему-то и unknown\\nочень много». Его оценка до этого: самая первая версия работала лучше поздних\\nисправлений, поэтому выбран именно этот baseline. Однако текущий звонок показывает,\\nчто даже baseline не решает задачу устойчиво.\\n\\nНаблюдения по тексту:\\n\\nПодсчёт именно напечатанных строк (не всех VAD/worker jobs):\\n\\n| Метка | Строк |\\n| --- | ---: |\\n| Me | 23 |\\n| Unknown | 13 |\\n| Speaker 1 | 11 |\\n| Speaker 3 | 2 |\\n| Speaker 4 | 1 |\\n| Speaker 5 | 1 |\\n| Всего | 51 |\\n\\nИз28строк системного источника13имеют Unknown. Это частота метки в данном выводе,\\nа не ошибка диаризации/DER: истинные личности и пропущенные фразы не размечены.\\n\\n- Видны Speaker1, Speaker3, Speaker4, Speaker5. Speaker2 в присланных строках нет.\\n  Он мог быть создан внутренне без напечатанного текста: ASR/фильтр могут подавить\\n  результат. Это гипотеза, а не подтверждение конкретного события.\\n- Первый видимый Speaker3 —1:55, Speaker4 —3:32, Speaker5 —4:04.\\n- Частые Unknown есть и на содержательных фразах, а не только на одиночных звуках.\\n- Повторился подозрительный `Me HY: Հովհ. EN: John: I know.` в0:58. Без аудио\\n  нельзя независимо установить, был ли это шум, кашель, речь или другая причина.\\n- Ошибки ASR и перевода остаются отдельными от ошибок меток. Английский текст\\n  не является эталоном распознанной армянской речи.\\n- Нет записи аудио, правильного текста, разметки личности говорящего для каждой\\n  строки, диагностических similarity scores и финального capture summary.\\n- Точное фактическое число удалённых говорящих и время их смены **в этом звонке**\\n  не указано. В более ранних проверках планировались два удалённых собеседника,\\n  но это не заменяет ground truth последнего звонка.\\n- Метрики DER, accuracy идентичностей, WER этого звонка и реальную задержку\\n  по такому текстовому выводу честно вычислить нельзя.\\n\\n## Полный лог, присланный пользователем\\n\\nСохранён без исправления слов, меток и переводов:\\n\\n```text\\nCombined live active. ## assistant source line 507

```
Расширенный контроль показал риск и у регистрации от 1.5 с: после синтетической смены полосы три голоса получили шесть ID и возникло одно присвоение чужому человеку. В коротких смешанных окнах ошибки есть и у baseline. Снижение порога длины это не решает.

Поэтому эти кандидаты оставляю только в эксперименте. Сейчас добавлю недостающие сравнения каждой половины с известными ID и сокращу диагностический вывод. Это позволит проверить следующую правку на твоих источниках, сохранив данные о её рисках.

## assistant source line 662

```
Проверка с настоящими FastConformer и NLLB тоже завершилась. На трёх повторах твоих отрывков baseline создал один ID и выдал 6 частей Unknown. Экспериментальный вариант создал два ID и выдал 0 частей Unknown. В обоих режимах завершились все 12 задач, временные WAV удалены.

Это улучшение на указанных отрывках, а не подтверждение качества звонков. В протокол включу и этот результат, и найденные ошибки кандидатов на смене канала и смешанной речи.

```

Все следующие inference checks offline.\n\n## Что удалось воспроизвести\n\nРеальный Silero, прежняя конфигурация, mono16k PCM, известная1s тишина вокруг каждого\nотрывка; resampling через PyAV. A даёт сегменты6.0,6.0,3.248s, B —**1.648s**.\nТишина/pre-roll входят в PCM длительность, не объявляются размеченной речью.\nПовтор A/B трижды, registry не сбрасывается. Это12 jobs и50.688s VAD PCM, не50s\nнезависимых наблюдений. Прямые файлы не моделируют Bluetooth/WASAPI/громкость Windows.\n\nBaseline создаёт только Speaker1: B не может создать ID при1.648s. Ещё6 ячеек A\nостаются Unknown из-за half gate. Совпадения отдельных половин с centroid теперь\nвидны в opt-in событии `half_matches`, вычисленном **до** создания/обновления ID.\n\n## Проверенные варианты, включая отрицательные результаты\n\n`scripts/check_speaker_candidates.py` проводит ablation на прежних12 evaluation\nutterances LibriSpeech, трёх corpus speaker ID; длительности1/1.264/1.52/1.968/2/4s,\ngain, synthetic band300–3400Hz, pre-roll, AB/BA, overlap и короткие смеси25/50/75%.\nБез подбора cosine threshold по ошибкам;0.47/margin0.08/capacity8 сохранены. Кэш native embeddings используется только\nв offline probe; время вычислений из него не является benchmark.\n\n- Регистрация от1.25s убирает Unknown на чистой серии1.264s, но создаёт4ID для3голосов.\n- Регистрация от1.5s на clean1.52s даёт3ID и0Unknown, но после band-смены —6ID\n  для3голосов,3дубликата и1.52s присвоения другому человеку. Однооконный embedding не разделяет\n  людей внутри окна. В коротком trial дополнительно создан ID смешанного окна.\n\nМетрики отчёта разделены: `wrong_person_s`, `mixed_single_label_s`, `mixed_new_ids`,\n`duplicate_ids`, `duplicate_s`, `unknown_s`. Соседние реально совпавшие labels объединяются\nпо прежнему правилу.\n\nДиагностический терминальный JSON сокращён: без повторения всех source anchors;\nсохраняет время/длину/ID/причину/best/second/halves/counts/probe_kind/experimental.\nПолное numeric event по-прежнему получает optional observer. `half_matches` —\npre-update, чтобы не сравнивать половины с только что созданным из них ID.\nОбычный вывод без diagnostics не получает новых событий.\n\n## Результат на предоставленных источниках\n\n`scripts/check_user_sources.py` проверяет baseline и trial непосредственно через\nproduction SpeakerTracker и сравнивает labels с offline candidate. For table header rows, use the fill and text colors specified in the table guidance below.\r\n- Visuals: Consider using tables, diagrams, and other visual components when they improve comprehension, navigation, or usability.\r\n- Tables:\r\n  - Use tables intentionally and only for these purposes:\r\n    - Comparing multiple items across the same set of attributes.\r\n    - Presenting numeric data, metrics, specifications, pricing, dates, or other values readers need to scan across.\r\n    - Showing a compact matrix, such as options × criteria, roles × responsibilities, or risks × mitigations.\r\n    - Presenting repeated records with a consistent schema.\r\n  - Keep long explanations, research findings, and proposed policy language in prose under descriptive headings. Use a compact matrix to summarize fields readers need to compare. Review consecutive table pages and replace tables that merely arrange narrative paragraphs into cells. Keep long tables only when readers need the full set of comparable records together.\r\n  - Suggestions:\r\n    - Set deliberate table/cell widths and heights instead of defaulting to full page width.\r\n    - Choose column widths intentionally rather than giving every column equal width by default. Very short fields (for example: item number, checkbox, score, result, year, date, or status) should usually be kept compact, while wider columns should be reserved for longer content.\r\n    - Avoid overly wide tables, and leave generous side margins so the layout feels natural.\r\n    - Keep all text vertically centered and make deliberate horizontal alignment choices.\r\n    - Ensure cell height avoids a crowded look. Leave clear vertical spacing between a table and its caption or following text.\r\n  - Hard constraints:\r\n    - Borders: Explicitly set outer and internal cell borders to light gray (`#D9D9D9`) so every table has visible borders.\r\n    - Header colors: Choose light gray, dark gray, dark blue, or light blue header fills to suit the document; do not default every table to light gray. Keep related tables consistent. Use white header text on dark fills and black text on light fills.\r\n    - Row shading: With a dark gray or dark blue header, alternate body-row backgrounds between white and a pale gray or pale blue tint. Keep the light gray borders visible.\r\n    - To prevent clipping/overflow:\r\n      - Never use fixed row heights that can truncate text; allow rows to expand with wrapped content.\r\n      - Ensure cell padding and line spacing are sufficient so descenders/ascenders don't get clipped.\r\n      - If content is tight, prefer (in order): wrap text -> adjust column widths -> reduce font slightly -> abbreviate headers/use two-line headers.\r\n    - Padding / breathing room: Ensure text doesn't sit against cell borders or look \"pinned\" to the upper-left. Favor generous internal padding on all sides, and keep it consistent across the table.\r\n    - Vertical alignment: In general, you should center your text vertically. Make sure that the content uses the available cell space naturally rather than clustering at the top.\r\n    - Horizontal alignment: Do not default all body cells to top-left alignment. Choose horizontal alignment intentionally by column type: centered alignment often works best for short values, status fields, dates, numbers, and check indicators; left alignment is usually better for narrative or multi-line text.\r\n    - Line height inside cells: Use line spacing that avoids a cramped feel and prevents ascenders/descenders from looking clipped. If a cell feels tight, adjust wrapping/width/padding before shrinking type.\r\n    - Width + wrapping sanity check: Avoid default equal-width columns when the content in each column clearly has different sizes. Avoid lines that run so close to the right edge that the cell feels overfull. If this happens, prefer wrapping or column-width adjustments before reducing font size.\r\n    - Spacing around tables: Keep clear separation between tables and surrounding text (especially the paragraph immediately above/below) so the layout doesn't feel stuck together. Captions and tables should stay visually paired, with deliberate spacing.\r\n    - Quick visual QA pass: Look for text that appears \"boundary-hugging\", specifically content pressed against the top or left edge of a cell or sitting too close beneath a table. Also watch for overly narrow descriptive columns and short-value columns whose contents feel awkwardly pinned. Correct these issues through padding, alignment, wrapping, or small column-width adjustments.\r\n- Forms / questionnaires: Design these as a usable form, not a spreadsheet.\r\n  - Prioritize clear response options, obvious and well-sized check targets, readable scale labels, generous row height, clear section hierarchy, light visual structure. Please size fields and columns based on the content they hold rather than by equal-width table cells.\r\n  - Use spacing, alignment, and subtle header/section styling to organize the page. Avoid dense full-grid borders, cramped layouts, and ambiguous numeric-only response areas.\r\n- Coherence vs. fragmentation: In general, try to keep things to be one coherent representation rather than fragmented, if possible.\r\n  - For example, don't split one logical dataset across multiple independent tables unless there's a clear, labeled reason.\r\n  - For example, if a table must span across pages, continue to the next page with a repeated header and consistent column order\r\n- Callouts: Do not use callout boxes, shaded note cards, accent-bar blocks, or boxed summaries and decision panels. Present this content as ordinary paragraphs, optionally with a bold lead-in. This applies whether the callout is built with a table, text box, shape, or paragraph shading/borders.\r\n- Spacing: Please check rigorously for spacing issues. Please always use a natural amount of spacing between adjacent components. Use clear, generous vertical spacing between sections and paragraphs, and leave a bit of extra space between subheadings and the content that follows when it improves readability. Use indentation and alignment intentionally so the document's hierarchy is immediately clear. At the same time, avoid large \"layout gaps\" caused by a table or chart not fitting at the bottom of a page and getting pushed to the next one. If this happens, please try these suggestions:\r\n  - moving the preceding paragraph(s) with it to the next page to keep the narrative cohesive\r\n  - scaling the visual modestly or simplify labels without hurting readability, formatting, or aesthetics of the visual\r\n  - Splitting the table/figure cleanly across multiple pages, but use repeated headers to make the page continuation clear.\r\n- Text boxes: For text boxes, please follow the same breathing-room rules as the tables: make sure to use generous internal padding, intentional alignment, and sufficient line spacing so text never feels cramped, clipped, or pinned to the edges. Keep spacing around the text box clear so it remains visually distinct from surrounding content, and if the content feels tight, prefer adjusting box size, padding, or text wrapping before reducing font size.\r\n- Layout/archetype: Remember to choose the right document archetype/template (proposal, SOP, workflow, form, handbook, etc.). Use a coherent style system. Once a style system is chosen, apply it consistently across headings, spacing, table treatments, and accent usage. If appropriate to the document type, include a cover page or front-matter elements such as title, subtitle, metadata, or branding.\r\n\r\n### Note on page sizing\r\n\r\nWhen creating a new DOCX, **always** default to the Letter size 8.5 x 11 inches, in Portrait orientation, unless the user specifies otherwise.\r\n\r\n### Note on font sizing\r\n\r\nUse a readable size appropriate to the text's role and typeface; ~11-12 pt is a good default for sustained prose. Use text 10 pt and below only if ideal for secondary roles or constrained tables/forms, and only when it remains comfortable at normal print or fit-width viewing. Do not shrink type merely to meet a page-count or compactness target. Follow explicit user typography instructions, but never at the expense of practical readability.\r\n\r\n### Editing tasks (DOCX edits) — apply instead of major rewrite behavior\r\n\r\nWhen the user asks to edit an existing document, preserve the original and make minimal, local changes:\r\n\r\n- Prefer inline edits (small replacements) over rewriting whole paragraphs.\r\n- Use clear inline annotations/comments at the point of change (margin comments or comment markers). Don’t move all feedback to the end.\r\n- Keep the original structure unless there’s a strong reason; if a restructure is needed, do it surgically and explain via comments.\r\n- Don’t “cross out everything and rewrite”; avoid heavy, blanket deletions. The goal is trackable improvements, not a fresh draft unless explicitly requested.\r\n\r\n## Equations: native Word math vs rendered fallback\r\n\r\nWhen the requested document or source contains mathematical equations, choose the equation\r\nrepresentation deliberately. Never leave raw LaTeX in the document or approximate structured\r\nnotation with plain text.\r\n\r\n1. **Prefer native Word equations (OMML, such as `<m:oMath>` or `<m:oMathPara>`)** when the user\r\n   asks for native or editable equations, when an existing DOCX already uses native equations, or\r\n   when equations need to remain searchable, accessible, copyable, inline with prose, or easy to\r\n   revise. Use native equations only through a tested OMML authoring path, and verify that Word and\r\n   the final LibreOffice render preserve the notation correctly.\r\n2. **Use the rendered MathJax fallback below** when native/editable math is not required and either\r\n   no reliable OMML authoring path is available or a complex display equation needs predictable\r\n   visual fidelity across renderers. This path produces an image, not a native Word equation. It is\r\n   best for stable display equations where portability matters more than editability.\r\n\r\nDo not silently rasterize an equation when the user explicitly requires native or editable Word\r\nmath. If no tested OMML path is available, explain that limitation rather than mislabeling an image\r\nas native. When editing an existing DOCX, preserve its equation representation unless the request or\r\nrender QA gives a clear reason to change it.\r\n\r\n### Rendered fallback: MathJax to high-resolution PNG\r\n\r\nThe standard artifact container includes Node.js, `mathjax-full`, `sharp`, and `python-docx`. Use\r\nMathJax to render LaTeX to SVG, then rasterize it to a high-resolution transparent PNG for reliable\r\ninsertion with `python-docx` and reliable LibreOffice rendering:\r\n\r\n```javascript\r\n\"use strict\";\r\n\r\nconst sharp = require(\"sharp\");\r\n\r\nlet _mathjax;\r\nlet _adaptor;\r\nlet _doc;\r\n\r\nfunction ensureMathJax() {\r\n  if (_mathjax && _adaptor && _doc) return;\r\n  const { mathjax } = require(\"mathjax-full/js/mathjax.js\");\r\n  const { TeX } = require(\"mathjax-full/js/input/tex.js\");\r\n  const { SVG } = require(\"mathjax-full/js/output/svg.js\");\r\n  const { liteAdaptor } = require(\"mathjax-full/js/adaptors/liteAdaptor.js\");\r\n  const { RegisterHTMLHandler } = require(\"mathjax-full/js/handlers/html.js\");\r\n  const { AllPackages } = require(\"mathjax-full/js/input/tex/AllPackages.js\");\r\n\r\n  _adaptor = liteAdaptor();\r\n  RegisterHTMLHandler(_adaptor);\r\n  const tex = new TeX({ packages: AllPackages });\r\n  const out = new SVG({ fontCache: \"local\" });\r\n  _doc = mathjax.document(\"\", { InputJax: tex, OutputJax: out });\r\n  _mathjax = mathjax;\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction latexToSvgDataUri(latex, display = true) {\r\n  ensureMathJax();\r\n  const html = _adaptor.outerHTML(_doc.convert(latex, { display }));\r\n  const a = html.indexOf(\"<svg\");\r\n  const b = html.indexOf(\"</svg>\");\r\n  let svg = a !== -1 && b !== -1 ? html.slice(a, b + 6) : html;\r\n  svg = svg.replace(/<\\?xml[^>]*>/g, \"\");\r\n  if (!/xmlns=\"http:\\/\\/www\\.w3\\.org\\/2000\\/svg\"/.test(svg)) {\r\n    svg = svg.replace(/<svg /, '<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" ');\r\n  }\r\n  svg = svg.replace(/(width|height)=\"([0-9.]+)(ex|em)\"/g, (_m, attr, num) => {\r\n    const px = Math.round(parseFloat(num) * 8.5);\r\n    return `${attr}=\"${px}px\"`;\r\n  });\r\n  svg = svg.replace(/currentColor/g, \"#000000\");\r\n  return \"data:image/svg+xml;base64,\" + Buffer.from(svg).toString(\"base64\");\r\n}\r\n\r\nasync function latexToPng(latex, outputPath, display = true) {\r\n  const dataUri = latexToSvgDataUri(latex, display);\r\n  const svg = Buffer.from(dataUri.split(\",\", 2)[1], \"base64\");\r\n  await sharp(svg, { density: 300 }).png().toFile(outputPath);\r\n}\r\n\r\nlatexToPng(\r\n  String.raw`\\int_{-\\infty}^{\\infty} e^{-x^2}\\,dx = \\sqrt{\\pi}`,\r\n  \"/mnt/data/equation.png\",\r\n).catch((error) => {\r\n  console.error(error);\r\n  process.exit(1);\r\n});\r\n```\r\n\r\nInsert the PNG at an intentional physical size without stretching it:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom docx import Document\r\nfrom docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH\r\nfrom docx.shared import Inches\r\n\r\ndoc = Document()\r\nparagraph = doc.add_paragraph()\r\nparagraph.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER\r\nparagraph.add_run().add_picture(\"/mnt/data/equation.png\", width=Inches(2.6))\r\ndoc.save(\"/mnt/data/output/equations.docx\")\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse `String.raw` for LaTeX strings so JavaScript preserves backslashes. Choose `display=true` for\r\nstandalone equations and `display=false` for compact inline-style expressions. After using either\r\nnative OMML or the rendered fallback, run the normal `render_docx.py` workflow and inspect every\r\nequation in the rendered page PNGs for missing glyphs, clipping, blur, poor sizing, or bad page\r\nbreaks.\r\n\r\n## Quick start (common one-liners)\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n# 1) Render any DOCX to PNGs (visual QA)\r\npython render_docx.py input.docx --output_dir out\r\n\r\n# 2) Remove reviewer comments (finalization)\r\npython scripts/comments_strip.py input.docx --out no_comments.docx\r\n\r\n# 3) Accept tracked changes (finalization)\r\npython scripts/accept_tracked_changes.py input.docx --mode accept --out accepted.docx\r\n\r\n# 4) Accessibility audit (+ optional safe fixes)\r\npython scripts/a11y_audit.py input.docx\r\npython scripts/a11y_audit.py input.docx --out_json a11y_report.json\r\npython scripts/a11y_audit.py input.docx --fix_image_alt from_filename --out a11y_fixed.docx\r\n\r\n# 5) Redact sensitive text (layout-preserving by default)\r\npython scripts/redact_docx.py input.docx redacted.docx --emails --phones\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Package layout\r\n\r\nThis skill is organized for progressive discovery: start here, then jump into task- or OOXML-specific docs.\r\n\r\nDOCS SKILL PACKAGE\r\n\r\nRoot:\r\n- SKILL.md: short overview + routing\r\n- manifest.txt: machine-readable list of files to download (one relative path per line)\r\n- render_docx.py: canonical DOCX→PNG renderer (container-safe LO profile + writable HOME + verbose logs)\r\n\r\nTasks:\r\n- tasks/read_review.md\r\n- tasks/create_edit.md\r\n- tasks/verify_render.md\r\n- tasks/accessibility_a11y.md\r\n- tasks/comments_manage.md\r\n- tasks/protection_restrict_editing.md\r\n- tasks/privacy_scrub_metadata.md\r\n- tasks/multi_doc_merge.md\r\n- tasks/style_lint_normalize.md\r\n- tasks/forms_content_controls.md\r\n- tasks/captions_crossrefs.md\r\n- tasks/redaction_anonymization.md\r\n- tasks/clean_tracked_changes.md\r\n- tasks/compare_diff.md\r\n- tasks/templates_style_packs.md\r\n- tasks/watermarks_background.md\r\n- tasks/footnotes_endnotes.md\r\n- tasks/fixtures_edge_cases.md\r\n- tasks/navigation_internal_links.md\r\n\r\nOOXML:\r\n- ooxml/tracked_changes.md\r\n- ooxml/comments.md\r\n- ooxml/hyperlinks_and_fields.md\r\n- ooxml/rels_and_content_types.md\r\n\r\nTroubleshooting:\r\n- troubleshooting/libreoffice_headless.md\r\n- troubleshooting/run_splitting.md\r\n\r\nScripts:\r\n\r\n**Core building blocks (importable helpers):**\r\n- `scripts/docx_ooxml_patch.py` — low-level OOXML patch helper (tracked changes, comments, hyperlinks, relationships). Other scripts reuse this.\r\n- `scripts/fields_materialize.py` — materialize `SEQ`/`REF` field *display text* for deterministic headless rendering/QA.\r\n\r\n**High-leverage utilities (also importable, but commonly invoked as CLIs):**\r\n- `render_docx.py` — canonical DOCX → PNG renderer (optional PDF via `--emit_pdf`; do not deliver intermediates unless asked).\r\n- `scripts/render_and_diff.py` — render + per-page image diff between two DOCXs.\r\n- `scripts/content_controls.py` — list / wrap / fill Word content controls (SDTs) for forms/templates.\r\n- `scripts/captions_and_crossrefs.py` — insert Caption paragraphs for tables/figures + optional bookmarks around caption numbers.\r\n- `scripts/insert_ref_fields.py` — replace `[[REF:bookmark]]` markers with real `REF` fields (cross-references).\r\n- `scripts/internal_nav.py` — add internal navigation links (static TOC + Top/Bottom + figN/tblN jump links).\r\n- `scripts/style_lint.py` — report common formatting/style inconsistencies.\r\n- `scripts/style_normalize.py` — conservative cleanup (clear run-level overrides; optional paragraph overrides).\r\n- `scripts/redact_docx.py` — layout-preserving redaction/anonymization.\r\n- `scripts/privacy_scrub.py` — remove personal metadata + `rsid*` attributes.\r\n- `scripts/set_protection.py` — restrict editing (read-only / comments / forms).\r\n- `scripts/comments_extract.py` — extract comments to JSON (text, author/date, resolved flag, anchored snippets).\r\n- `scripts/comments_strip.py` — remove all comments (final-delivery mode).\r\n\r\n**Audits / conversions / niche helpers:**\r\n- `scripts/fields_report.py`, `scripts/heading_audit.py`, `scripts/section_audit.py`, `scripts/images_audit.py`, `scripts/footnotes_report.py`, `scripts/watermark_audit_remove.py`\r\n- `scripts/xlsx_to_docx_table.py`, `scripts/docx_table_to_csv.py`\r\n- `scripts/insert_toc.py`, `scripts/insert_note.py`, `scripts/apply_template_styles.py`, `scripts/accept_tracked_changes.py`, `scripts/make_fixtures.py`\r\n\r\n**v7 additions (stress-test helpers):**\r\n- `scripts/watermark_add.py` — add a detectable VML watermark object into an existing header.\r\n- `scripts/comments_add.py` — add multiple comments (by paragraph substring match) and wire up comments.xml plumbing if needed.\r\n- `scripts/comments_apply_patch.py` — append/replace comment text and mark/clear resolved state (`w:done=1`).\r\n- `scripts/add_tracked_replacements.py` — generate tracked-change replacements (`<w:del>` + `<w:ins>`) in-place.\r\n- `scripts/a11y_audit.py` — audit a11y issues; can also apply simple fixes via `--fix_table_headers` / `--fix_image_alt`.\r\n- `scripts/flatten_ref_fields.py` — replace REF/PAGEREF field blocks with their cached visible text for deterministic rendering.\r\n\r\n> `scripts/xlsx_to_docx_table.py` also marks header rows as repeating headers (`w:tblHeader`) to improve a11y and multi-page tables.\r\n\r\nExamples:\r\n- examples/end_to_end_smoke_test.md\r\n\r\n> Note: `manifest.txt` is **machine-readable** and is used by download tooling. It must contain only relative file paths (one per line).\r\n\r\n\r\n## Coverage map (scripts ↔ task guides)\r\n\r\nThis is a quick index so you can jump from a helper script to the right task
